memory_candidates.content: In a Lean repo whose sorry-debt ratchet strips block comments (/- ... -/, including /-- ... -/) before counting code-position \bsorry\b occurrences, that ratchet doubles as a comment-delimiter-breakage detector for docstring-only edits. A comment-only change must leave the per-file sorry count bit-identical; any movement means a /- or -/ delimiter broke and prose is now being elaborated as code. This makes an otherwise-expensive full build unnecessary as the per-phase gate for annotation-correction work -- run the cheap census after every hunk and reserve the full build for the final gate. Verified against cslib's scripts/check-sorry-suppressions.sh, whose header documents the comment-stripping discrimination rule.
